title: Chemical Labelling
summary: Labels on hazardous chemicals must show standard elements: product identifier, signal word, hazard statements, precautionary statements, pictograms, and the supplier's contact information. The label is a quick alert, and the SDS has the full details.
talking_points: Every container of a hazardous chemical must have a label with six elements: product identifier, signal word, hazard statement(s), precautionary statement(s), pictogram(s), and the supplier's name, address, and phone number.
There are only two signal words. "Danger" is for the more severe hazards and "Warning" is for the less severe. Only one appears on a label.
Hazard statements describe the nature and degree of the hazard. The same hazard has the same statement on any chemical label.
Precautionary statements tell you how to prevent or respond to exposure, and how to store and dispose of the chemical.
A pictogram is a black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point. A red frame with no symbol is not allowed.
Labels are limited in space. Check the Safety Data Sheet for full details.
The product identifier on the label matches Section 1 of the SDS.
OSHA enforces eight of the nine GHS pictograms. The environmental pictogram is not mandatory but may appear.
site_hazards_to_check: Containers with missing, torn, or unreadable labels
Labels missing a signal word, pictogram, or supplier contact
No Safety Data Sheet available to match the label
Crew who do not know what the label pictograms mean
discussion_questions: What are the two signal words, and which one means the more severe hazard?
What does the pictogram on this container tell us?
Where can we find more details when the label runs out of space?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA published material. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: Verified against OSHA 3636 (HazCom labels and pictograms brief): six label elements, only two signal words (Danger more severe, Warning less) with only one on a label, hazard statements standardized, precautionary statements, red square frame set on a point with black symbol on white and empty red frame not permitted, product identifier matches SDS Section 1, OSHA enforces eight of nine GHS pictograms (environmental not mandatory).
Citations: 29 CFR 1926.59 (structurer-added) exists and applies HazCom to construction, correct; 1910.1200 is the text the source cites and applies to construction through 1926.59.

Non-blocking: the point that precautionary statements cover storage and disposal is in the source. Talk does not cover workplace secondary-container labelling rules (1910.1200(f)(6)); site_hazards mention unlabeled containers as a hazard only.
